extracted.intended_audience: USCIS/immigration adjudicators, immigration attorneys, advocates, and affected noncitizens
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, definitions, exemptions, and procedural guidance governing DHS/USCIS determinations under the public charge ground of inadmissibility (INA §212(a)(4)) including outreach, training, applicability, exemptions, waivers, and definitional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public communications must avoid undue confusion; DHS will conduct robust outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS intends that the final rule should be communicated so it 'faithfully applies the public charge ground of inadmissibility without causing undue confusion among the public.' DHS is planning a robust communication effort in conjunction with and immediately following the publication of this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will conduct outreach and produce public-facing materials; commenters recommended funding trusted community organizations for 'know your rights' presentations, hotlines, phone banks, social media engagement, and train-the-trainer presentations; DHS considered those recommendations but noted new grant programs are outside the scope of the rulemaking while taking them under advisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear public statement that COVID-19 testing/treatment/vaccination not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not consider receipt of treatments or preventative services related to COVID-19, including vaccinations, in a public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes it has clarified in the regulatory text that benefits not referenced in 8 CFR 212.21(b) or (c) — including benefits related to immunizations or testing for communicable diseases — will not be considered; DHS will reiterate this in follow-on guidance and outreach materials even though such outreach materials are not part of the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and policy guidance for adjudicators to ensure consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS plans to provide training to officers to ensure consistency in adjudications and will issue policy guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual that includes information from the NPRM and the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended significant investment in training/retraining immigration officers and caseworkers; DHS will provide a 'solid foundation' on public charge determinations via training and will publish updated Policy Manual guidance accessible to applicants, officers, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: No blanket disclosure requirement for extensions or changes of status
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not require, as a condition of an application or petition for extension of stay or change of status, that a nonimmigrant disclose the use of public benefits since obtaining the nonimmigrant status they wish to extend or change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS concluded the burden of such an inquiry outweighs the benefit because such conditions would apply to few nonimmigrants and many nonimmigrants are barred from receiving many public benefits considered in this rule (e.g., SSI, TANF, long-term institutional Medicaid). Concerns about self-reliance for nonimmigrants are addressed by initial eligibility requirements and application requirements for those statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge ground applies only to applicants for visas, admission, and adjustment of status unless Congress exempts them
rubrics_metrics.description: The public charge ground of inadmissibility applies to all applicants for visas, admission, and adjustment of status unless exempted from the ground by Congress (as reflected in 8 CFR 212.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain requests such as withholding of removal, parole, suspension of deportation, Deferred Enforced Departure, and deferred action are not applications for visas/admission/adjustment and therefore are not subject to the public charge ground; DHS will list exemptions and a 'catch-all' in 8 CFR 212.23 to reflect statutory exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of benefits received while in a status that is exempt from public-charge
rubrics_metrics.description: It is consistent with Congressional intent for DHS to not consider public benefits received by noncitizens during periods in which they were present in an immigration category that is exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility (e.g., refugees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will exclude from consideration benefits that an applicant received while in a status exempt from the ground, because Congress intended such vulnerable populations to be able to receive benefits without risking adverse immigration consequences. By contrast, DHS will consider benefits received by other categories (e.g., parolees, withholding recipients) when they apply in a category subject to public charge, because Congress has not expressed an intention to exclude those benefit uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions listed in regulation reflect Congress's designations; DHS will not add exemptions beyond statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions in 8 CFR 212.23 reflect classes of noncitizens that Congress has designated as exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters' requests to add categories (e.g., withholding of removal, parole, DED, DACA, deferred action) to the exemptions list were declined where those categories are not applications for visas/admission/adjustment; DHS will update Policy Manual guidance as appropriate but cannot create statutory exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children are not presumptively exempt; age is one statutory factor in totality of circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS disagrees with a presumption that children are not likely at any time to become public charges; an applicant's age is one of the statutory minimum factors DHS must consider as part of a public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS must make a predictive assessment 'likely at any time' including the period soon after admission/adjustment; Congress did not create a general exemption for children, so DHS will consider statutory minimum factors and current/past receipt of benefits in the totality of the circumstances and will 'favorably consider a sufficient Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A' as a positive factor. DHS will provide guidance to officers on applying the rule for children given their particular circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support under §213A is a positive factor
rubrics_metrics.description: A sufficient Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA is a positive factor that makes an applicant less likely at any time to become a public charge in the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will consider an appropriate affidavit as mitigating factor when assessing likelihood under the totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions for VAWA self-petitioners and certain 'qualified aliens' apply regardless of pathway to LPR status
rubrics_metrics.description: If a noncitizen 'is a VAWA self-petitioner' or 'is a qualified alien described in' 8 U.S.C. 1641(c), INA sec. 212(a)(4)(A)-(C) shall not apply to them; this exemption does not depend on the pathway to lawful permanent resident status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS clarified regulatory text to reflect that statutory exemptions for VAWA and qualified-aliens are controlling; the exemptions in INA sec. 212(a)(4)(E) do not apply to INA sec. 212(a)(4)(D) (Affidavit of Support requirement). DHS will not change statutory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers limited to those Congress established; DHS may not expand waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: The waivers listed in 8 CFR 212.23(c) reflect the classes of noncitizens Congress has designated as eligible to seek a waiver of inadmissibility; only Congress can establish additional waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters' requests to create waivers for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking who did not seek VAWA/TVPA protections were declined; current waivers include applicants for admission as S nonimmigrants and INA sec. 212(d)(3) nonimmigrant waivers, among others Congress has specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: T and U nonimmigrant exemptions require valid status at filing and during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: For the statutory exemptions to apply (e.g., T and U nonimmigrants), DHS interprets the present-tense statutory language to mean the noncitizen must hold and be in valid T or U nonimmigrant status at the time Form I-485 is properly filed and throughout the pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because U and T status is granted for a finite period and can be revoked, DHS views the exemption as applying while the noncitizen 'is' in that status; if they no longer are in that status at filing or adjudication, the exemption does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'likely at any time to become a public charge' (core definitional standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS defines 'likely at any time to become a public charge' to mean 'likely at any time to become primarily dependent on the government for subsistence, as demonstrated by either the receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS believes this definition achieves necessary clarity; officers have applied a similar standard for over 20 years. DHS also defines 'public cash assistance for income maintenance' and 'long-term institutionalization at government expense' in regulation to implement this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge determination is prospective and subjective; 'likely' interpreted as 'more likely than not'
rubrics_metrics.description: The public charge inadmissibility determination is necessarily prospective ('likely at any time') and inherently subjective ('in the opinion of' DHS). DHS continues the 2019 Final Rule interpretation of 'likely' as 'more likely than not.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declines to further define 'likely' beyond this interpretation, reasoning that the statutory language and existing practice provide sufficient guidance for officers performing the fact-specific discretionary determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers must consider statutory minimum factors and totality of circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In making public charge inadmissibility determinations, DHS will consider the statutory minimum factors as set forth in the rule and the applicant's current and past receipt of public benefits in the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS emphasizes consideration of all statutory minimum factors (including age, health, family status, assets/resources/financial status, education/skills) and will issue policy guidance to assist officers in faithfully applying the statute and the rule.
